title: Route Economics Atlas: deterministic per-route/model/customer rollup service
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: downstream console views and finance reports require a deterministic, explainable rollup of cost and latency broken down by route, model variant, and customer tenant. Current rollups are expensive to recompute, divergent across services, and lack stable attribution when model variants or kernel mappings change.

Goal: build the Route Economics Atlas (Atlas) — a centralized backend service that consumes normalized runtime telemetry and produces immutable daily and hourly rollups that are: deterministic across replays, linked to runtime span evidence, and cheaply queryable by Console and billing pipelines. Atlas should support reconciliation (replaying with deterministic seeds), schema evolution for new telemetry fields, and fine-grained lineage metadata so Console can show "why" a number changed between versions.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: hourly and daily deterministic rollups per (route, model_version, tenant, region), causal links to runtime spans, compact storage format (columnar + provenance index), APIs for Console and billing services, migration plan for existing rollups.
- Out of scope: realtime per-request costing for low-latency RU decisions (will be handled by inference-side microservices), ad-hoc per-token forensic queries spanning months (may be supported later via export).

Core design principles: deterministic transforms, provenance-first (link numbers back to trace/span IDs), cost-agnostic math (allow swapping unit-cost inputs), and ability to re-run a rollup deterministically when runtime kernel mappings or quantization profiles change.
acceptance_criteria: Atlas consumes normalized telemetry events (v2) from telemetry-topic and completes an hourly run within SLA (90% of hours finish within 45 minutes)
Each leaderboard entry is annotated with provenance: list of sample runtime span IDs and the deterministic hash used to attribute tokens
APIs: GET /atlas/v1/rollup?route=X&model=Y&tenant=Z&start=... returns identical results for a given rollup_id and is paginated
Console integration: Console dashboard queries the Atlas API for per-route breakdowns and shows model-variant, kernel, and quantization contributions
Reconciliation: Running Atlas with a recorded seed on the same telemetry slice produces bit-for-bit identical rollups (end-to-end deterministic replay)
Migration: a one-time backfill plan is defined and validated for the last 90 days of data with estimated cost and time

2026-01-18 — Miguel Santos: Prototype completed for deterministic attribution using sample-based prefix hashing. Proof-run on a 24h test slice produced stable attributions across replay with variance <0.1% compared to golden metrics.

2026-01-22 — Lina Cho (PM): Reviewed prototype results. PM request: expose model-variant and kernel_id breakdowns separately so Console can show "cost delta due to kernel change". Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-01-28 — Security review kickoff: security team requested threat model for provenance links; explicit authorization required to access span-level evidence. Adding KMS envelope for provenance index encryption.

2026-02-02 — Engineering review: Decided on columnar Parquet-like format with a small provenance Bloom index to avoid heavy lookups. Trade-off: saves storage but requires controlled size sampling for trace links. Action: implement sampled-span retention policy and api surface for full trace exports behind RBAC.
2026-02-04 — Miguel Santos: Initial API spec and OpenAPI draft posted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/atlas/blob/main/api/openapi.yml. Reviewing with Console team next week.
tech_notes:
Implementation plan: (1) Ingest normalized telemetry (ingestion job with idempotent dedupe + schema validation), (2) Attribution engine: deterministic sharder + token-slicing algorithm to map spans->routes, (3) Rollup compute (map-reduce style) producing hourly and daily artifacts, (4) Provenance index: sampled span registry with deterministic hashes, (5) Storage: columnar blobs in object store + small metadata store for rollup manifest, (6) Read API service with role-based access and caching layer for Console.

Operational considerations: backfill window handling (fast-path parallel compute), incremental rollups when cost-weights change, monitoring (run duration, failed partitions, drift from runtime telemetry), and autoscaling needs during backfills.

Performance targets: target 6x speedup over current naive batch job via sharding and local aggregation; memory footprint must cap <6GB per worker in the 95th percentile.

Security notes: provenance links expose span ids; only return sample lists to Console and require enterprise role for full trace exports. Use KMS for metadata encryption and audit every full-export request.
migration_plan: Phase 1: pilot on one high-traffic route for 7 days, validate parity with current billing numbers. Phase 2: backfill 30 days for top 20 routes, run reconciliation tooling and compare. Phase 3: schedule full 90-day backfill during low-traffic weekend with parallel workers and quota bump. Coordinate with Billing and Console teams for cutover date and read-side feature flags.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deterministic replay may diverge due to missing telemetry fields. Mitigation: strict schema validation and filler tokens for missing fields, plus alerting on schema drift.
Risk: Storage of provenance links increases cost. Mitigation: sampled retention + bloom index + HSM/KMS-protected export of full traces only on request.
Risk: Backfill compute spikes causing quota issues. Mitigation: throttled parallelism and scheduler that respects cluster capacity; run long backfills during maintenance windows.
